🌍 Pezeshkian says no power can destroy Iran

📌 New York, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian says that no power can destroy Iran as the country has deep historical roots.

Pezeshkian made the remarks in reaction to recent anti-Iran remarks by US President Donald Trump, while speaking to Iranian journalists in New York on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday.
​
Pezeshkian said Washington was pursuing a force-based approach in different parts of the world, stressing that US actions were incompatible with international law and humanitarian principles.
​
Pezeshkian pointed to US actions involving Venezuela, Cuba, and Greenland, saying such an approach had not previously been expressed so openly, as the US even speaks of the destruction of a country.
​
He said Iran has deep historical roots and cannot be destroyed, adding that the Iranian people have remained present on the field despite all the pressure they had faced.

🌍 Iran saw inaction, not neutrality, during recent war: Pezeshkian

📌 New York, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian told European Council President Antonio Costa on Wednesday that Iran had seen inaction rather than neutrality from some countries during the recent war, calling on European states to reconsider their approach and maintain greater independence.

Meeting on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York, Pezeshkian said European countries deprived themselves of a role in international developments by aligning with hostile US actions.
​
He criticized Europe’s approach to the snapback mechanism and the 2015 Iran nuclear deal, saying European governments’ positions reduced their ability to influence international developments. He also referred to comments by the NATO secretary general about European countries’ assistance to the United States during the war and called for a reassessment of European policies.
​
Pezeshkian said regional security should be the responsibility of countries in the region, stressing that Western intervention has adversely affected security beyond the region.
​
Costa called for a European role in addressing regional issues, while Pezeshkian said Europe’s alignment with Washington had limited its ability to play such a role.
​
In a separate meeting with Armenia’s prime minister in New York, Pezeshkian stressed Iran’s policy of expanding cooperation with neighboring and regional countries, with implementation of bilateral agreements, particularly on regional transit routes, among the government’s priorities.
​
The Armenian prime minister also stressed the need to accelerate implementation of bilateral agreements, saying they would contribute to regional development and peace.
